"Score how well this research card fits each existing programme below. Each programme lists claims about its current practice; two checkers fetched each source and marked each claim SUPPORTED, PARTIAL, UNSUPPORTED, CONTRADICTED or UNREACHABLE. Rely only on claims that at least one checker marked SUPPORTED or PARTIAL. Score each programme 1-5 on each criterion, with a reason of at most 25 words. Decide only from the text below; do not use tools.
Root question: Industrial food ingredient replacement for sustainability? Industrial food recipe replacement for sustainability?
Card:
**FD1 · Industrial food ingredient replacement for sustainability.** seed pick · compute tested: yes · plan expects: the lever · REJECT

**Question.** Does increasing the capacity of a neural ingredient-substitution model measurably improve its ranking of sustainable replacements, measured as Hit@1 on Recipe1MSubs [src_gismo_sizes]?

**What is known.** Rita 2024 fine-tuned GPT-3.5 and TinyLlama on Recipe1MSubs, lifting Hit@1 from 34.53 to 38.03; no capacity sweep within one protocol exists [src_llm]. Whether ranking quality keeps rising with model capacity inside one fixed protocol on Recipe1MSubs is unmeasured; the only scaling evidence is cross-protocol.

**Hypothesis.** More capacity in a substitution ranker improves substitution ranking because larger encoders capture finer ingredient context, as LLM results suggest [src_llm].

**If compute is the lever.** Hit@1 rises with width, reaching at least 22 percent at width 512, above GISMo's 20.56, and still climbing.

**If not.** Hit@1 plateaus near GISMo's 20.56 at every width; extra capacity adds nothing, so wider models are not the lever.

**Test.** Reproduce GISMo's Recipe1MSubs result, then train the ranker at four widths 64, 128, 256, 512 with five seeds each on four GPUs; if Hit@1 climbs past the 20.56 baseline with width, compute is the lever.

*Compute axis.* Substitution-ranker capacity (ingredient-encoder embedding width): 64–512 dimension, 4 levels. Closest prior: not on this axis.

*Restructuring.* none.

**Check first.** Reproduce GISMo's published test-set MRR of 31.51 and Hit@1 of 20.56 using the official code, within 2 MRR points [src_gismo_gismo]. Tolerance: plus or minus 2.0 MRR points (mean over 5 seeds).

**Would not show.** Shows ranking accuracy on home recipes, not industrial formulations, and never measures actual environmental footprint or sensory quality of the substitute.

*Cost.* Plans $104.48 of the $1,000 budget over 22 machine-hours, leaving $895.52. Main guess: wall-clock per training run on one A100 40GB [g], measured after $24.88 of spend; the budget is reached if it is 20× higher.

[SUPPORTED, SUPPORTED]\",\"GISMo's published Recipe1MSubs test result — MRR 31.51 and Hit@1 20.56, averaged over 5 runs — is the exact baseline the card's 'Check first' reproduction targets. [SUPPORTED, SUPPORTED]\",\"The model is implemented in PyTorch with the Deep Graph Library (DGL) for sparse graph operations, over a 6,653-ingredient FlavorGraph-derived vocabulary and the ~49k-pair Recipe1MSubs training split — the scale and tooling the card would reuse. [SUPPORTED, SUPPORTED]\",\"The project is an archived, read-only open-source benchmark (Meta AI authors), not an actively developed product, and GISMo feeds a personalized inverse-cooking (image-to-recipe) pipeline. [SUPPORTED, SUPPORTED]\"],\"if_lever_changes\":\"It would overturn the project's fixed-width default: the archived 300-dim GIN ingredient encoder would be shown to leave ranking quality on the table, so any future GISMo-style substitution ranker (including the personalized inverse-cooking integration) should scale the ingredient-encoder width; width would become a published scaling curve rather than an untested hyperparameter.\",\"if_not_changes\":\"It would confirm GISMo's 300-dim ingredient encoder was already at the plateau, validating the original fixed-width configuration and telling future work to seek gains from graph structure, context, or training data (the paper's own ablations) rather than from model capacity.\",\"already_done\":{\"status\":\"partly\",\"claim\":\"Meta only ever trained and evaluated GISMo at a single ingredient-encoder width (hidden=300, emb_d=300); the paper's 5-run average is at that one width and no 64–512 sweep exists in the paper or repo.\",\"checks\":[\"CONTRADICTED\",\"CONTRADICTED\"]}}
{\"programme\":2,\"name\":\"Imperial College London — Veselkov Lab / Hyperfoods (Rita et al. 2024, iAnalytica)\",\"step\":\"The GISMo baseline/reimplementation step of their ingredient-substitution pipeline: they re-run GISMo as the benchmark ranker against which fine-tuned LLMs (DaVinci, TinyLlama, GPT-3.5) are compared, so the card's width axis targets this baseline ranker's ingredient-encoder width.\",\"practice\":[\"They re-implemented and re-ran GISMo as their benchmark, fixing the ingredient embedding dimension at 300 with two 300-hidden-unit graph convolutional layers, a dropout of 0.25, and 400 epochs with negative sampling. [SUPPORTED, SUPPORTED]\",\"Their reimplemented GISMo baseline scores Hit@1 34.53 ± 0.10% on the original Recipe1MSubs, and fine-tuned GPT-3.5-Turbo-1106 lifts this to 38.03 ± 0.28%, while TinyLlama-1.1B reaches only 20.93 ± 0.29%. [SUPPORTED, SUPPORTED]\",\"The work sits inside the Hyperfoods ERC programme (coordinated by Imperial College London), which applies graph-based ML to computationally design personalised nutrition and which funded Rita et al. [SUPPORTED, SUPPORTED]\",\"The re-run GISMo and fine-tuned models (plus the dataset-filtering and fine-tuning scripts) are released on the iAnalytica Bitbucket repository, so the card's width-sweep could be reproduced against their released baseline. [SUPPORTED, SUPPORTED]\"],\"if_lever_changes\":\"Their headline comparison would be confounded: they conclude LLMs beat GISMo (38.03 vs 34.53 Hit@1) against a GISMo baseline fixed at 300 dim, so if a wider GISMo keeps climbing that baseline is under-parameterized and they would need to re-benchmark GPT-3.5/TinyLlama against a width-scaled GISMo before attributing the gain to LLM capability; their phytochemically-enriched recipe-generation step would inherit whichever ranker actually wins.\",\"if_not_changes\":\"Their 300-dim GISMo baseline stands as a fair reference, so the LLM advantage (GPT-3.5-Turbo's 38.03 Hit@1) is a real model effect rather than a capacity artifact; this strengthens their choice of fine-tuned LLMs for generating phytochemically enriched substitutions and lets them skip a wider GISMo.\",\"already_done\":{\"status\":\"no\",\"claim\":\"Rita et al. re-implemented GISMo at a single 300-dim embedding width (averaged over 5 runs) and swept model families (DaVinci/TinyLlama/GPT-3.5), but never swept the GISMo encoder width across 64–512.\",\"checks\":[\"SUPPORTED\",\"SUPPORTED\"]}}
Criteria:
fit: Does the card's measured outcome feed a named step of this programme? 5 = it measures the quantity that step's current practice depends on, on systems the programme uses; 3 = it feeds that step only through a stand-in (another model, system or scale) the programme would have to bridge; 1 = no step of the programme would use the outcome.
change: What would the card's outcomes change in this programme's practice? 5 = either outcome changes a choice the programme makes now (what to build, buy, label, check or scale), as its supported practice shows; 3 = only one outcome would change practice, or the change needs further work the card does not do; 1 = neither outcome would change what the programme does.
new: Has this programme, or work it relies on, already answered the card's question? 5 = supported claims show its current practice lacks this measurement; 3 = unclear, or partly answered; 1 = already answered.
Return only JSON: {\"scores\": [{\"programme\": 1, \"criterion\": \"fit | change | new\", \"value\": 1, \"reason\": \"\"}]}"
